388	    def _validate_config(self):
389	        config = self.config
390	        # number of GPUs total
391	        n_gpus = config.trainer.n_gpus_per_node * config.trainer.nnodes
392	        if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == "megatron":
393	            model_parallel_size = (
394	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size
395	                * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size
396	            )
397	            assert (
398	                n_gpus % (model_parallel_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size) == 0
399	            ), (
400	                f"n_gpus ({n_gpus}) must be divisible by model_parallel_size ({model_parallel_size}) times "
401	                f"context_parallel_size ({config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size})"
402	            )
403	            megatron_dp = n_gpus // (
404	                model_parallel_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size
405	            )
406	            minimal_bsz = megatron_dp * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
407	        else:
408	            minimal_bsz = n_gpus
409	
410	        # 1. Check total batch size for data correctness
411	        real_train_batch_size = config.data.train_batch_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n
412	        assert real_train_batch_size % minimal_bsz == 0, (
413	            f"real_train_batch_size ({real_train_batch_size}) must be divisible by minimal possible batch size "
414	            f"({minimal_bsz})"
415	        )
416	
417	        # A helper function to check "micro_batch_size" vs "micro_batch_size_per_gpu"
418	        # We throw an error if the user sets both. The new convention is "..._micro_batch_size_per_gpu".
419	        def check_mutually_exclusive(mbs, mbs_per_gpu, name: str):
420	            """Validate mutually exclusive micro batch size configuration options.
421	
422	            Ensures that users don't set both deprecated micro_batch_size and
423	            the new micro_batch_size_per_gpu parameters simultaneously.
424	
425	            Args:
426	                mbs: Deprecated micro batch size parameter value.
427	                mbs_per_gpu: New micro batch size per GPU parameter value.
428	                name (str): Configuration section name for error messages.
429	
430	            Raises:
431	                ValueError: If both parameters are set or neither is set.
432	            """
433	            settings = {
434	                "actor_rollout_ref.actor": "micro_batch_size",
435	                "critic": "micro_batch_size",
436	                "reward_model": "micro_batch_size",
437	                "actor_rollout_ref.ref": "log_prob_micro_batch_size",
438	                "actor_rollout_ref.rollout": "log_prob_micro_batch_size",
439	            }
440	
441	            if name in settings:
442	                param = settings[name]
443	                param_per_gpu = f"{param}_per_gpu"
444	
445	                if mbs is None and mbs_per_gpu is None:
446	                    raise ValueError(
447	                        f"[{name}] Please set at least one of '{name}.{param}' or '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'."
448	                    )
449	
450	                if mbs is not None and mbs_per_gpu is not None:
451	                    raise ValueError(
452	                        f"[{name}] You have set both '{name}.{param}' AND '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'. Please remove "
453	                        f"'{name}.{param}' because only '*_{param_per_gpu}' is supported (the former is deprecated)."
454	                    )
455	
456	        if not config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz:
457	            # actor: ppo_micro_batch_size vs. ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
458	            check_mutually_exclusive(
459	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size,
460	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
461	                "actor_rollout_ref.actor",
462	            )
463	
464	            if self.use_reference_policy:
465	                # reference: log_prob_micro_batch_size vs. log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
466	                check_mutually_exclusive(
467	                    config.actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size,
468	                    config.actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
469	                    "actor_rollout_ref.ref",
470	                )
471	
472	            #  The rollout section also has log_prob_micro_batch_size vs. log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
473	            check_mutually_exclusive(
474	                config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size,
475	                config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
476	                "actor_rollout_ref.rollout",
477	            )
478	
479	        if self.use_critic and not config.critic.use_dynamic_bsz:
480	            # Check for critic micro-batch size conflicts
481	            check_mutually_exclusive(
482	                config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size, config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu, "critic"
483	            )
484	
485	        # Check for reward model micro-batch size conflicts
486	        if config.reward_model.enable and not config.reward_model.use_dynamic_bsz:
487	            check_mutually_exclusive(
488	                config.reward_model.micro_batch_size, config.reward_model.micro_batch_size_per_gpu, "reward_model"
489	            )
490	
491	        # Actor
492	        # check if train_batch_size is larger than ppo_mini_batch_size
493	        # if NOT dynamic_bsz, we must ensure:
494	        #    ppo_mini_batch_size is divisible by ppo_micro_batch_size
495	        #    ppo_micro_batch_size * sequence_parallel_size >= n_gpus
496	        if not config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz:
497	            assert config.data.train_batch_size >= config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size
498	            sp_size = config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1)

680	    def _validate(self):
681	        data_source_lst = []
682	        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
683	
684	        # Lists to collect samples for the table
685	        sample_inputs = []
686	        sample_outputs = []
687	        sample_scores = []
688	        sample_turns = []
689	
690	        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
691	            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)
692	
693	            # repeat test batch
694	            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
695	                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
696	            )
697	
698	            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
699	            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
700	                return {}
701	
702	            # Store original inputs
703	            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
704	            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
705	            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
706	            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
707	
708	            batch_keys_to_pop = ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "position_ids"]
709	            non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop = ["raw_prompt_ids"]
710	            for key in ["multi_modal_data", "raw_prompt", "tools_kwargs", "interaction_kwargs", "agent_name"]:
711	                if key in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
712	                    non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop.append(key)
713	            test_gen_batch = test_batch.pop(
714	                batch_keys=batch_keys_to_pop,
715	                non_tensor_batch_keys=non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop,
716	            )
717	
718	            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {
719	                "eos_token_id": self.tokenizer.eos_token_id,
720	                "pad_token_id": self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
721	                "recompute_log_prob": False,
722	                "do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample,
723	                "validate": True,
724	                "global_steps": self.global_steps,
725	            }
726	            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")
727	
728	            # pad to be divisible by dp_size
729	            size_divisor = (
730	                self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
731	                if not self.async_rollout_mode
732	                else self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
733	            )
734	            test_gen_batch_padded, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(test_gen_batch, size_divisor)
735	            if not self.async_rollout_mode:
736	                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)
737	            else:
738	                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)
739	
740	            # unpad
741	            test_output_gen_batch = unpad_dataproto(test_output_gen_batch_padded, pad_size=pad_size)
742	
743	            print("validation generation end")
744	
745	            # Store generated outputs
746	            output_ids = test_output_gen_batch.batch["responses"]
747	            output_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in output_ids]
748	            sample_outputs.extend(output_texts)
749	
750	            test_batch = test_batch.union(test_output_gen_batch)
751	            test_batch.meta_info["validate"] = True
752	
753	            # evaluate using reward_function
754	            result = self.val_reward_fn(test_batch, return_dict=True)
755	            reward_tensor = result["reward_tensor"]
756	            scores = reward_tensor.sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
757	            sample_scores.extend(scores)
758	
759	            response_length = test_batch.batch["attention_mask"].sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
760	            reward_extra_infos_dict["response_length"].extend(response_length)
761	
762	            reward_extra_infos_dict["reward"].extend(scores)
763	            print(f"len reward_extra_infos_dict['reward']: {len(reward_extra_infos_dict['reward'])}")
764	            if "reward_extra_info" in result:
765	                for key, lst in result["reward_extra_info"].items():
766	                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key].extend(lst)
767	                    print(f"len reward_extra_infos_dict['{key}']: {len(reward_extra_infos_dict[key])}")
768	
769	            # collect num_turns of each prompt
770	            if "__num_turns__" in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
771	                sample_turns.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["__num_turns__"])
772	
773	            data_source_lst.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch.get("data_source", ["unknown"] * reward_tensor.shape[0]))
774	
775	        self._maybe_log_val_generations(inputs=sample_inputs, outputs=sample_outputs, scores=sample_scores)
776	
777	        # dump generations
778	        val_data_dir = self.config.trainer.get("validation_data_dir", None)
779	        if val_data_dir:
780	            self._dump_generations(
781	                inputs=sample_inputs,
782	                outputs=sample_outputs,
783	                scores=sample_scores,
784	                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_dict,
785	                dump_path=val_data_dir,
786	            )
787	
788	        for key_info, lst in reward_extra_infos_dict.items():
789	            assert len(lst) == 0 or len(lst) == len(sample_scores), f"{key_info}: {len(lst)=}, {len(sample_scores)=}"
790	
791	        data_sources = np.concatenate(data_source_lst, axis=0)
792	
793	        data_src2var2metric2val = process_validation_metrics(data_sources, sample_inputs, reward_extra_infos_dict)
794	        metric_dict = {}
795	        for data_source, var2metric2val in data_src2var2metric2val.items():
796	            core_var = "acc" if "acc" in var2metric2val else "reward"
797	            for var_name, metric2val in var2metric2val.items():
798	                n_max = max([int(name.split("@")[-1].split("/")[0]) for name in metric2val.keys()])
799	                for metric_name, metric_val in metric2val.items():
800	                    if (
801	                        (var_name == core_var)
802	                        and any(metric_name.startswith(pfx) for pfx in ["mean", "maj", "best"])
803	                        and (f"@{n_max}" in metric_name)
804	                    ):
805	                        metric_sec = "val-core"
806	                    else:
807	                        metric_sec = "val-aux"
808	                    pfx = f"{metric_sec}/{data_source}/{var_name}/{metric_name}"
809	                    metric_dict[pfx] = metric_val
810	
811	        if len(sample_turns) > 0:
812	            sample_turns = np.concatenate(sample_turns)
813	            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/min"] = sample_turns.min()
814	            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/max"] = sample_turns.max()
815	            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/mean"] = sample_turns.mean()
816	
817	        return metric_dict

819	    def init_workers(self):
820	        """Initialize distributed training workers using Ray backend.
821	
822	        Creates:
823	        1. Ray resource pools from configuration
824	        2. Worker groups for each role (actor, critic, etc.)
825	        """
826	        self.resource_pool_manager.create_resource_pool()
827	
828	        self.resource_pool_to_cls = {pool: {} for pool in self.resource_pool_manager.resource_pool_dict.values()}
829	
830	        # create actor and rollout
831	        if self.hybrid_engine:
832	            resource_pool = self.resource_pool_manager.get_resource_pool(Role.ActorRollout)
833	            actor_rollout_cls = RayClassWithInitArgs(
834	                cls=self.role_worker_mapping[Role.ActorRollout],
835	                config=self.config.actor_rollout_ref,
836	                role="actor_rollout",
837	                profile_option=self.config.trainer.npu_profile.options,
838	            )
839	            self.resource_pool_to_cls[resource_pool]["actor_rollout"] = actor_rollout_cls
840	        else:
841	            raise NotImplementedError
842	
843	        # create critic
844	        if self.use_critic:
845	            resource_pool = self.resource_pool_manager.get_resource_pool(Role.Critic)
846	            critic_cls = RayClassWithInitArgs(cls=self.role_worker_mapping[Role.Critic], config=self.config.critic)
847	            self.resource_pool_to_cls[resource_pool]["critic"] = critic_cls
848	
849	        # create reference policy if needed
850	        if self.use_reference_policy:
851	            resource_pool = self.resource_pool_manager.get_resource_pool(Role.RefPolicy)
852	            ref_policy_cls = RayClassWithInitArgs(
853	                self.role_worker_mapping[Role.RefPolicy],
854	                config=self.config.actor_rollout_ref,
855	                role="ref",
856	                profile_option=self.config.trainer.npu_profile.options,
857	            )
858	            self.resource_pool_to_cls[resource_pool]["ref"] = ref_policy_cls
859	
860	        # create a reward model if reward_fn is None

864	            rm_cls = RayClassWithInitArgs(self.role_worker_mapping[Role.RewardModel], config=self.config.reward_model)
865	            self.resource_pool_to_cls[resource_pool]["rm"] = rm_cls
866	
867	        # initialize WorkerGroup
868	        # NOTE: if you want to use a different resource pool for each role, which can support different parallel size,
869	        # you should not use `create_colocated_worker_cls`.
870	        # Instead, directly pass different resource pool to different worker groups.
871	        # See https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/master/examples/ray/tutorial.ipynb for more information.
872	        all_wg = {}

876	        if OmegaConf.select(self.config.trainer, "profile_steps") is not None:

880	            )
881	            wg_kwargs["worker_nsight_options"] = OmegaConf.to_container(
882	                OmegaConf.select(self.config.trainer, "worker_nsight_options")
883	            )

885	        for resource_pool, class_dict in self.resource_pool_to_cls.items():

1008	    def _balance_batch(self, batch: DataProto, metrics, logging_prefix="global_seqlen"):
1009	        """Reorder the data on single controller such that each dp rank gets similar total tokens"""
1010	        attention_mask = batch.batch["attention_mask"]
1011	        batch_size = attention_mask.shape[0]
1012	        global_seqlen_lst = batch.batch["attention_mask"].view(batch_size, -1).sum(-1).tolist()  # (train_batch_size,)
1013	        world_size = self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
1014	        global_partition_lst = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(
1015	            global_seqlen_lst, k_partitions=world_size, equal_size=True
1016	        )
1017	        # reorder based on index. The data will be automatically equally partitioned by dispatch function
1018	        global_idx = torch.tensor([j for partition in global_partition_lst for j in partition])
1019	        batch.reorder(global_idx)
1020	        global_balance_stats = log_seqlen_unbalance(
1021	            seqlen_list=global_seqlen_lst, partitions=global_partition_lst, prefix=logging_prefix
1022	        )
1023	        metrics.update(global_balance_stats)

1028	                [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(batch.batch))], dtype=object
1029	            )

1031	        batch = batch.repeat(repeat_times=repeat_times, interleave=True)
1032	
1033	        # pop those keys for generation
1034	        batch_keys_to_pop = ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "position_ids"]

1037	            if key in batch.non_tensor_batch:
1038	                non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop.append(key)

1042	        )

1049	        batch, gen_batch = self._prepare_batch_for_rollout(batch, repeat_times)

1063	    def _compute_old_log_prob(self, compute_log_prob_fn: Callable, batch: DataProto):
1064	        old_log_prob = compute_log_prob_fn(batch)
1065	        entropys = old_log_prob.batch["entropys"]
1066	        response_masks = batch.batch["response_mask"]
1067	        loss_agg_mode = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode
1068	        entropy_agg = agg_loss(loss_mat=entropys, loss_mask=response_masks, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
1069	        old_log_prob_metrics = {"actor/entropy": entropy_agg.detach().item()}
1070	        old_log_prob.batch.pop("entropys")
1071	        batch = batch.union(old_log_prob)
1072	
1073	        if "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch.keys():
1074	            rollout_old_log_probs = batch.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
1075	            actor_old_log_probs = batch.batch["old_log_probs"]
1076	            responses = batch.batch["responses"]
1077	            response_mask = batch.batch["response_mask"]
1078	
1079	            rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
1080	            actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
1081	            rollout_probs_diff = actor_probs - rollout_probs
1082	            rollout_probs_diff = torch.masked_select(rollout_probs_diff, response_mask.bool())
1083	            rollout_probs_diff_abs = torch.abs(rollout_probs_diff)
1084	            rollout_probs_diff_max = torch.max(rollout_probs_diff)
1085	            rollout_probs_diff_min = torch.min(rollout_probs_diff)
1086	            rollout_probs_diff_mean = torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff_abs)
1087	            rollout_probs_diff_std = torch.std(rollout_probs_diff_abs)
1088	            actor_log_probs_min = torch.min(actor_old_log_probs * response_mask)
1089	            rollout_log_probs_min = torch.min(rollout_old_log_probs * response_mask)
1090	
1091	            masked_diff = (actor_probs - rollout_probs) * response_mask
1092	            max_diff_idx = torch.argmax(masked_diff)
1093	            max_diff_response_id = responses.flatten()[max_diff_idx]
1094	            min_diff_idx = torch.argmin(masked_diff)
1095	            min_diff_response_id = responses.flatten()[min_diff_idx]
1096	            print(f"max_diff_response_id: {max_diff_response_id}, {masked_diff.flatten()[max_diff_idx]}")
1097	            print(f"min_diff_response_id: {min_diff_response_id}, {masked_diff.flatten()[min_diff_idx]}")
1098	            rollout_probs_diff_0 = (actor_probs - rollout_probs)[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1099	            response_id_0 = responses[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1100	            response_mask_0 = response_mask[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1101	            first_rollout = []
1102	            for i in range(len(response_mask_0)):
1103	                if response_mask_0[i]:
1104	                    first_rollout.append((response_id_0[i], rollout_probs_diff_0[i]))
1105	            # print(f"The first rollout {first_rollout}")
1106	            old_log_prob_metrics.update(
1107	                {
1108	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": rollout_probs_diff_max.detach().item(),
1109	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_min": rollout_probs_diff_min.detach().item(),
1110	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": rollout_probs_diff_mean.detach().item(),
1111	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": rollout_probs_diff_std.detach().item(),
1112	                    "training/actor_log_probs_min": actor_log_probs_min.detach().item(),
1113	                    "training/rollout_log_probs_min": rollout_log_probs_min.detach().item(),
1114	                }
1115	            )
1116	        from run_support import parity_metrics
1117	        old_log_prob_metrics.update(parity_metrics(batch, self.global_steps))
1118	        return batch, old_log_prob_metrics

1121	        """
1122	        The training loop of PPO.
1123	        The driver process only need to call the compute functions of the worker group through RPC
1124	        to construct the PPO dataflow.
1125	        The light-weight advantage computation is done on the driver process.

import multiprocessing
import os
from functools import partial

import ray

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score


def _call_with_kwargs(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.

    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
    """
    merged_kwargs = {**kwargs, **extra_kwargs}
    return raw_fn(*args, **merged_kwargs)


def get_custom_reward_fn(config):
    """Load and return a custom reward function from external file.

    Dynamically imports a reward function from a specified file path and wraps
    it with additional keyword arguments from the configuration.

    Args:
        config (dict): Configuration dictionary containing custom_reward_function
                      settings with 'path', 'name', and 'reward_kwargs' fields.

    Returns:
        callable or None: Wrapped reward function with merged kwargs, or None
                         if no custom reward function is configured.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the specified reward function file doesn't exist.
        RuntimeError: If there's an error loading the module from file.
        AttributeError: If the specified function name isn't found in the module.
    """
    import importlib.util
    import sys

    reward_fn_config = config.get("custom_reward_function") or {}
    file_path = reward_fn_config.get("path")
    if not file_path:
        return None

    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Reward function file '{file_path}' not found.")

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("custom_module", file_path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    try:
        sys.modules["custom_module"] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error loading module from '{file_path}': {e}") from e

    function_name = reward_fn_config.get("name")
    if not hasattr(module, function_name):
        raise AttributeError(f"Reward function '{function_name}' not found in '{file_path}'.")

    print(f"using customized reward function '{function_name}' from '{file_path}'")
    raw_fn = getattr(module, function_name)

    reward_kwargs = dict(reward_fn_config.get("reward_kwargs", {}))

    return partial(_call_with_kwargs, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)


def load_reward_manager(config, tokenizer, num_examine, **reward_kwargs):
    """
    Load and initialize a reward manager based on the configuration.

    Args:
        config: PPO trainer configuration object containing reward_model fields.
        tokenizer: Tokenizer object used for processing text.
        num_examine: Number of samples to examine.
        **reward_kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the reward manager.

    Returns:
        An instance of the specified reward manager class.
    """
    from verl.workers.reward_manager import get_reward_manager_cls

    # The list of pre-defined reward managers are defined in `verl/workers/reward_manager/`:
    # naive: NaiveRewardManager
    # prime: PrimeRewardManager
    # batch: BatchRewardManager
    # dapo: DAPORewardManager
    # Note(haibin.lin): For custom reward managers, please make sure they are imported and
    # registered via `verl.workers.reward_manager.register`
    # By default reward_manager is set to naive (NaiveRewardManager)
    reward_manager_name = config.reward_model.get("reward_manager", "naive")
    reward_manager_cls = get_reward_manager_cls(reward_manager_name)

    # Try to get a custom reward function based on the configuration
    compute_score = get_custom_reward_fn(config)
    final_compute_score = compute_score

    if compute_score is None:
        sandbox_config = config.reward_model.get("sandbox_fusion")
        sandbox_url = sandbox_config.get("url") if sandbox_config else None
        memory_limit_mb = sandbox_config.get("memory_limit_mb", 1024)
        if sandbox_url:
            sandbox_manager = multiprocessing.Manager()
            # Create a semaphore to control concurrent access to the sandbox
            _concurrent_semaphore = sandbox_manager.Semaphore(sandbox_config.get("max_concurrent", 64))
            final_compute_score = partial(
                default_compute_score,
                sandbox_fusion_url=sandbox_url,
                concurrent_semaphore=_concurrent_semaphore,
                memory_limit_mb=memory_limit_mb,
            )
        else:
            final_compute_score = default_compute_score

    # Instantiate and return the reward manager with the specified parameters
    return reward_manager_cls(
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        num_examine=num_examine,
        compute_score=final_compute_score,
        reward_fn_key=config.data.reward_fn_key,
        **reward_kwargs,
    )


def compute_reward(data: DataProto, reward_fn):
    """
    Compute reward for a batch of data.
    Args:
        data: DataProto object containing the input data.
        reward_fn: Reward function to compute the reward.
    Returns:
        Tuple of reward tensor and extra info dictionary.
    """
    try:
        reward_result = reward_fn(data, return_dict=True)
        reward_tensor = reward_result["reward_tensor"]
        reward_extra_infos_dict = reward_result.get("reward_extra_info", {})
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error in reward_fn: {e}")
        reward_tensor = reward_fn(data)
        reward_extra_infos_dict = {}

    return reward_tensor, reward_extra_infos_dict


@ray.remote(num_cpus=1)
def compute_reward_async(data: DataProto, config=None, tokenizer=None, reward_fn=None):
    """
    Load the reward manager and compute the reward for a batch of data.
    This is meant to be run in a separate Ray worker.
    """
    if reward_fn is None:
        assert config is not None and tokenizer is not None, (
            "config and tokenizer must not be None when reward_fn is None"
        )
        import warnings

        warnings.warn("using config and tokenizer with compute_reward_async is deprecated", stacklevel=2)
        reward_fn = load_reward_manager(
            config, tokenizer, num_examine=0, **config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs", {})
        )

    return compute_reward(data, reward_fn)

"""
Note that we don't combine the main with ray_trainer as ray_trainer is used by other main.
"""

import os
import socket

import hydra
import ray
from omegaconf import OmegaConf

from verl.experimental.dataset.sampler import AbstractSampler
from verl.trainer.constants_ppo import PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV
from verl.trainer.ppo.ray_trainer import RayPPOTrainer
from verl.trainer.ppo.reward import load_reward_manager
from verl.utils.device import is_cuda_available
from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_type


@hydra.main(config_path="config", config_name="math_grpo", version_base=None)
def main(config):
    """Main entry point for PPO training with Hydra configuration management.

    Args:
        config_dict: Hydra configuration dictionary containing training parameters.
    """
    run_ppo(config)


# Define a function to run the PPO-like training process
def run_ppo(config) -> None:
    """Initialize Ray cluster and run distributed PPO training process.

    Args:
        config: Training configuration object containing all necessary parameters
                for distributed PPO training including Ray initialization settings,
                model paths, and training hyperparameters.
    """
    # Check if Ray is not initialized
    if not ray.is_initialized():
        # Initialize Ray with a local cluster configuration
        # Set environment variables in the runtime environment to control tokenizer parallelism,
        # NCCL debug level, VLLM logging level, and allow runtime LoRA updating
        # `num_cpus` specifies the number of CPU cores Ray can use, obtained from the configuration
        ray.init(
            runtime_env=PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV,
            num_cpus=config.ray_init.num_cpus,
        )

    # Create a remote instance of the TaskRunner class, and
    # Execute the `run` method of the TaskRunner instance remotely and wait for it to complete
    if (
        is_cuda_available
        and config.trainer.get("profile_steps") is not None
        and len(config.trainer.get("profile_steps", [])) > 0
    ):
        nsight_options = OmegaConf.to_container(config.trainer.controller_nsight_options)
        runner = TaskRunner.options(runtime_env={"nsight": nsight_options}).remote()
    else:
        runner = TaskRunner.remote()
    ray.get(runner.run.remote(config))

    # [Optional] get the path of the timeline trace file from the configuration, default to None
    # This file is used for performance analysis
    timeline_json_file = config.ray_init.get("timeline_json_file", None)
    if timeline_json_file:
        ray.timeline(filename=timeline_json_file)


@ray.remote(num_cpus=1)  # please make sure main_task is not scheduled on head
class TaskRunner:
    """Ray remote class for executing distributed PPO training tasks.

    This class encapsulates the main training logic and runs as a Ray remote actor
    to enable distributed execution across multiple nodes and GPUs.
    """

    def run(self, config):
        """Execute the main PPO training workflow.

        This method sets up the distributed training environment, initializes
        workers, datasets, and reward functions, then starts the training process.

        Args:
            config: Training configuration object containing all parameters needed
                   for setting up and running the PPO training process.
        """
        # Print the initial configuration. `resolve=True` will evaluate symbolic values.
        from pprint import pprint

        from omegaconf import OmegaConf

        from verl.utils.fs import copy_to_local

        print(f"TaskRunner hostname: {socket.gethostname()}, PID: {os.getpid()}")
        pprint(OmegaConf.to_container(config, resolve=True))
        OmegaConf.resolve(config)

        # Download the checkpoint from HDFS to the local machine.
        # `use_shm` determines whether to use shared memory, which could lead to faster model loading if turned on
        local_path = copy_to_local(
            config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path, use_shm=config.actor_rollout_ref.model.get("use_shm", False)
        )

        # Instantiate the tokenizer and processor.
        from verl.utils import hf_processor, hf_tokenizer

        trust_remote_code = config.data.get("trust_remote_code", False)
        tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(local_path, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code)
        # Used for multimodal LLM, could be None
        processor = hf_processor(local_path, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, use_fast=True)

        # Define worker classes based on the actor strategy.
        if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}:
            assert config.critic.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}
            from verl.single_controller.ray import RayWorkerGroup
            from verl.workers.fsdp_workers import ActorRolloutRefWorker, AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker, CriticWorker

            actor_rollout_cls = (
                AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker
                if config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode == "async"
                else ActorRolloutRefWorker
            )
            ray_worker_group_cls = RayWorkerGroup

        elif config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == "megatron":
            assert config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == config.critic.strategy
            from verl.single_controller.ray.megatron import NVMegatronRayWorkerGroup
            from verl.workers.megatron_workers import ActorRolloutRefWorker, AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker, CriticWorker

            actor_rollout_cls = (
                AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker
                if config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode == "async"
                else ActorRolloutRefWorker
            )
            ray_worker_group_cls = NVMegatronRayWorkerGroup

        else:
            raise NotImplementedError

        from verl.trainer.ppo.ray_trainer import ResourcePoolManager, Role

        # Map roles to their corresponding remote worker classes.
        role_worker_mapping = {
            Role.ActorRollout: ray.remote(actor_rollout_cls),
            Role.Critic: ray.remote(CriticWorker),
        }

        # Define the resource pool specification.
        # Map roles to the resource pool.
        global_pool_id = "global_pool"
        resource_pool_spec = {
            global_pool_id: [config.trainer.n_gpus_per_node] * config.trainer.nnodes,
        }
        mapping = {
            Role.ActorRollout: global_pool_id,
            Role.Critic: global_pool_id,
        }

        # We should adopt a multi-source reward function here:
        # - for rule-based rm, we directly call a reward score
        # - for model-based rm, we call a model
        # - for code related prompt, we send to a sandbox if there are test cases
        # finally, we combine all the rewards together
        # The reward type depends on the tag of the data
        if config.reward_model.enable:
            if config.reward_model.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}:
                from verl.workers.fsdp_workers import RewardModelWorker
            elif config.reward_model.strategy == "megatron":
                from verl.workers.megatron_workers import RewardModelWorker
            else:
                raise NotImplementedError
            role_worker_mapping[Role.RewardModel] = ray.remote(RewardModelWorker)
            mapping[Role.RewardModel] = global_pool_id

        # Add a reference policy worker if KL loss or KL reward is used.
        if config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward or config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss:
            role_worker_mapping[Role.RefPolicy] = ray.remote(ActorRolloutRefWorker)
            mapping[Role.RefPolicy] = global_pool_id

        # Load the reward manager for training and validation.
        reward_fn = load_reward_manager(
            config, tokenizer, num_examine=0, **config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs", {})
        )
        val_reward_fn = load_reward_manager(
            config, tokenizer, num_examine=1, **config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs", {})
        )
        resource_pool_manager = ResourcePoolManager(resource_pool_spec=resource_pool_spec, mapping=mapping)

        from verl.utils.dataset.rl_dataset import collate_fn

        # Create training and validation datasets.
        train_dataset = create_rl_dataset(config.data.train_files, config.data, tokenizer, processor, is_train=True)
        val_dataset = create_rl_dataset(config.data.val_files, config.data, tokenizer, processor, is_train=False)
        train_sampler = create_rl_sampler(config.data, train_dataset)

        # Initialize the PPO trainer.
        trainer = RayPPOTrainer(
            config=config,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            processor=processor,
            role_worker_mapping=role_worker_mapping,
            resource_pool_manager=resource_pool_manager,
            ray_worker_group_cls=ray_worker_group_cls,
            reward_fn=reward_fn,
            val_reward_fn=val_reward_fn,
            train_dataset=train_dataset,
            val_dataset=val_dataset,
            collate_fn=collate_fn,
            train_sampler=train_sampler,
            device_name=config.trainer.device,
        )
        # Initialize the workers of the trainer.
        trainer.init_workers()
        # Start the training process.
        trainer.fit()


def create_rl_dataset(data_paths, data_config, tokenizer, processor, is_train=True):
    """Create a dataset.

    Arguments:
        data_paths: List of paths to data files.
        data_config: The data config.
        tokenizer (Tokenizer): The tokenizer.
        processor (Processor): The processor.

    Returns:
        dataset (Dataset): The dataset.
    """
    from torch.utils.data import Dataset

    from verl.utils.dataset.rl_dataset import RLHFDataset

    # Check if a custom dataset class is specified in the data configuration
    # and if the path to the custom class is provided
    if "custom_cls" in data_config and data_config.custom_cls.get("path", None) is not None:
        # Dynamically load the custom dataset class
        dataset_cls = load_extern_type(data_config.custom_cls.path, data_config.custom_cls.name)
        # Verify that the custom dataset class inherits from torch.utils.data.Dataset
        if not issubclass(dataset_cls, Dataset):
            raise TypeError(
                f"The custom dataset class '{data_config.custom_cls.name}' from "
                f"'{data_config.custom_cls.path}' must inherit from torch.utils.data.Dataset"
            )
    elif "datagen" in data_config and data_config.datagen.get("path", None) is not None and is_train:
        # If a data generation strategy is specified, use the DynamicGenDataset class
        from verl.utils.dataset.dynamicgen_dataset import DynamicGenDataset

        dataset_cls = DynamicGenDataset
        print("Using DynamicGenDataset for data generation.")

    else:
        # Use the default RLHFDataset class if no custom class is specified
        dataset_cls = RLHFDataset
    print(f"Using dataset class: {dataset_cls.__name__}")

    # Instantiate the dataset using the determined dataset class
    dataset = dataset_cls(
        data_files=data_paths,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        processor=processor,
        config=data_config,
    )

    return dataset


def create_rl_sampler(data_config, dataset):
    """Create a sampler for the dataset.

    Arguments:
        data_config: The data config.
        dataset (Dataset): The dataset.

    Returns:
        sampler (Sampler): The sampler.
    """
    import torch
    from torch.utils.data import RandomSampler, SequentialSampler

    if data_config.sampler is not None and data_config.sampler.get("class_path", None) is not None:
        curriculum_class = load_extern_type(
            data_config.sampler.class_path,
            data_config.sampler.class_name,
        )
        sampler = curriculum_class(
            data_source=dataset,
            data_config=data_config,
        )
        assert isinstance(sampler, AbstractSampler)
        assert data_config.get("dataloader_num_workers", 8) == 0, (
            "If using curriculum, num_workers must be 0 to prevent data caching. "
            "If the dataloader caches data before the batch is done the "
            "curriculum sampler won't have the opportunity to reorder it. "
        )

    # Use a sampler to facilitate checkpoint resumption.
    # If shuffling is enabled in the data configuration, create a random sampler.
    elif data_config.shuffle:
        train_dataloader_generator = torch.Generator()
        train_dataloader_generator.manual_seed(data_config.get("seed", 1))
        sampler = RandomSampler(data_source=dataset, generator=train_dataloader_generator)
    else:
        # If shuffling is disabled, use a sequential sampler to iterate through the dataset in order.
        sampler = SequentialSampler(data_source=dataset)

    return sampler


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

33	@hydra.main(config_path="config", config_name="math_grpo", version_base=None)
34	def main(config):
35	    """Main entry point for PPO training with Hydra configuration management.
36	
37	    Args:
38	        config_dict: Hydra configuration dictionary containing training parameters.
39	    """
40	    run_ppo(config)

43	# Define a function to run the PPO-like training process
44	def run_ppo(config) -> None:
45	    """Initialize Ray cluster and run distributed PPO training process.
46	
47	    Args:
48	        config: Training configuration object containing all necessary parameters
49	                for distributed PPO training including Ray initialization settings,
50	                model paths, and training hyperparameters.
51	    """
52	    # Check if Ray is not initialized
53	    if not ray.is_initialized():
54	        # Initialize Ray with a local cluster configuration
55	        # Set environment variables in the runtime environment to control tokenizer parallelism,
56	        # NCCL debug level, VLLM logging level, and allow runtime LoRA updating
57	        # `num_cpus` specifies the number of CPU cores Ray can use, obtained from the configuration
58	        ray.init(
59	            runtime_env=PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV,
60	            num_cpus=config.ray_init.num_cpus,
61	        )
62	
63	    # Create a remote instance of the TaskRunner class, and
64	    # Execute the `run` method of the TaskRunner instance remotely and wait for it to complete
65	    if (
66	        is_cuda_available
67	        and config.trainer.get("profile_steps") is not None
68	        and len(config.trainer.get("profile_steps", [])) > 0
69	    ):
70	        nsight_options = OmegaConf.to_container(config.trainer.controller_nsight_options)
71	        runner = TaskRunner.options(runtime_env={"nsight": nsight_options}).remote()
72	    else:
73	        runner = TaskRunner.remote()
74	    ray.get(runner.run.remote(config))
75	
76	    # [Optional] get the path of the timeline trace file from the configuration, default to None
77	    # This file is used for performance analysis
78	    timeline_json_file = config.ray_init.get("timeline_json_file", None)
79	    if timeline_json_file:
80	        ray.timeline(filename=timeline_json_file)

83	@ray.remote(num_cpus=1)  # please make sure main_task is not scheduled on head
84	class TaskRunner:
85	    """Ray remote class for executing distributed PPO training tasks.
86	
87	    This class encapsulates the main training logic and runs as a Ray remote actor
88	    to enable distributed execution across multiple nodes and GPUs.
89	    """
90	
91	    def run(self, config):
92	        """Execute the main PPO training workflow.
93	
94	        This method sets up the distributed training environment, initializes
95	        workers, datasets, and reward functions, then starts the training process.
96	
97	        Args:
98	            config: Training configuration object containing all parameters needed
99	                   for setting up and running the PPO training process.
100	        """
101	        # Print the initial configuration. `resolve=True` will evaluate symbolic values.
102	        from pprint import pprint
103	
104	        from omegaconf import OmegaConf
105	
106	        from verl.utils.fs import copy_to_local
107	
108	        print(f"TaskRunner hostname: {socket.gethostname()}, PID: {os.getpid()}")
109	        pprint(OmegaConf.to_container(config, resolve=True))
110	        OmegaConf.resolve(config)
111	
112	        # Download the checkpoint from HDFS to the local machine.
113	        # `use_shm` determines whether to use shared memory, which could lead to faster model loading if turned on
114	        local_path = copy_to_local(
115	            config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path, use_shm=config.actor_rollout_ref.model.get("use_shm", False)
116	        )
117	
118	        # Instantiate the tokenizer and processor.
119	        from verl.utils import hf_processor, hf_tokenizer
120	
121	        trust_remote_code = config.data.get("trust_remote_code", False)
122	        tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(local_path, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code)
123	        # Used for multimodal LLM, could be None
124	        processor = hf_processor(local_path, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, use_fast=True)
125	
126	        # Define worker classes based on the actor strategy.
127	        if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}:
128	            assert config.critic.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}
129	            from verl.single_controller.ray import RayWorkerGroup
130	            from verl.workers.fsdp_workers import ActorRolloutRefWorker, AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker, CriticWorker
131	
132	            actor_rollout_cls = (
133	                AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker
134	                if config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode == "async"
135	                else ActorRolloutRefWorker
136	            )
137	            ray_worker_group_cls = RayWorkerGroup
138	
139	        elif config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == "megatron":
140	            assert config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == config.critic.strategy
141	            from verl.single_controller.ray.megatron import NVMegatronRayWorkerGroup
142	            from verl.workers.megatron_workers import ActorRolloutRefWorker, AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker, CriticWorker
143	
144	            actor_rollout_cls = (
145	                AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker
146	                if config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode == "async"
147	                else ActorRolloutRefWorker
148	            )
149	            ray_worker_group_cls = NVMegatronRayWorkerGroup
150	
151	        else:
152	            raise NotImplementedError
153	
154	        from verl.trainer.ppo.ray_trainer import ResourcePoolManager, Role
155	
156	        # Map roles to their corresponding remote worker classes.
157	        role_worker_mapping = {
158	            Role.ActorRollout: ray.remote(actor_rollout_cls),
159	            Role.Critic: ray.remote(CriticWorker),
160	        }
161	
162	        # Define the resource pool specification.
163	        # Map roles to the resource pool.
164	        global_pool_id = "global_pool"
165	        resource_pool_spec = {
166	            global_pool_id: [config.trainer.n_gpus_per_node] * config.trainer.nnodes,
167	        }
168	        mapping = {
169	            Role.ActorRollout: global_pool_id,
170	            Role.Critic: global_pool_id,
171	        }
172	
173	        # We should adopt a multi-source reward function here:
174	        # - for rule-based rm, we directly call a reward score
175	        # - for model-based rm, we call a model
176	        # - for code related prompt, we send to a sandbox if there are test cases
177	        # finally, we combine all the rewards together
178	        # The reward type depends on the tag of the data
179	        if config.reward_model.enable:
180	            if config.reward_model.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}:
181	                from verl.workers.fsdp_workers import RewardModelWorker
182	            elif config.reward_model.strategy == "megatron":
183	                from verl.workers.megatron_workers import RewardModelWorker
184	            else:
185	                raise NotImplementedError
186	            role_worker_mapping[Role.RewardModel] = ray.remote(RewardModelWorker)
187	            mapping[Role.RewardModel] = global_pool_id
188	
189	        # Add a reference policy worker if KL loss or KL reward is used.
190	        if config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward or config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss:
191	            role_worker_mapping[Role.RefPolicy] = ray.remote(ActorRolloutRefWorker)
192	            mapping[Role.RefPolicy] = global_pool_id
193	
194	        # Load the reward manager for training and validation.
195	        reward_fn = load_reward_manager(
196	            config, tokenizer, num_examine=0, **config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs", {})
197	        )
198	        val_reward_fn = load_reward_manager(
199	            config, tokenizer, num_examine=1, **config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs", {})
200	        )
201	        resource_pool_manager = ResourcePoolManager(resource_pool_spec=resource_pool_spec, mapping=mapping)
202	
203	        from verl.utils.dataset.rl_dataset import collate_fn
204	
205	        # Create training and validation datasets.
206	        train_dataset = create_rl_dataset(config.data.train_files, config.data, tokenizer, processor, is_train=True)
207	        val_dataset = create_rl_dataset(config.data.val_files, config.data, tokenizer, processor, is_train=False)
208	        train_sampler = create_rl_sampler(config.data, train_dataset)
209	
210	        # Initialize the PPO trainer.
211	        trainer = RayPPOTrainer(
212	            config=config,
213	            tokenizer=tokenizer,
214	            processor=processor,
215	            role_worker_mapping=role_worker_mapping,
216	            resource_pool_manager=resource_pool_manager,
217	            ray_worker_group_cls=ray_worker_group_cls,
218	            reward_fn=reward_fn,
219	            val_reward_fn=val_reward_fn,
220	            train_dataset=train_dataset,
221	            val_dataset=val_dataset,
222	            collate_fn=collate_fn,
223	            train_sampler=train_sampler,
224	            device_name=config.trainer.device,
225	        )
226	        # Initialize the workers of the trainer.
227	        trainer.init_workers()
228	        # Start the training process.
229	        trainer.fit()

232	def create_rl_dataset(data_paths, data_config, tokenizer, processor, is_train=True):
233	    """Create a dataset.
234	
235	    Arguments:
236	        data_paths: List of paths to data files.
237	        data_config: The data config.
238	        tokenizer (Tokenizer): The tokenizer.
239	        processor (Processor): The processor.
240	
241	    Returns:
242	        dataset (Dataset): The dataset.
243	    """
244	    from torch.utils.data import Dataset
245	
246	    from verl.utils.dataset.rl_dataset import RLHFDataset
247	
248	    # Check if a custom dataset class is specified in the data configuration
249	    # and if the path to the custom class is provided
250	    if "custom_cls" in data_config and data_config.custom_cls.get("path", None) is not None:
251	        # Dynamically load the custom dataset class
252	        dataset_cls = load_extern_type(data_config.custom_cls.path, data_config.custom_cls.name)
253	        # Verify that the custom dataset class inherits from torch.utils.data.Dataset
254	        if not issubclass(dataset_cls, Dataset):
255	            raise TypeError(
256	                f"The custom dataset class '{data_config.custom_cls.name}' from "
257	                f"'{data_config.custom_cls.path}' must inherit from torch.utils.data.Dataset"
258	            )
259	    elif "datagen" in data_config and data_config.datagen.get("path", None) is not None and is_train:
260	        # If a data generation strategy is specified, use the DynamicGenDataset class
261	        from verl.utils.dataset.dynamicgen_dataset import DynamicGenDataset
262	
263	        dataset_cls = DynamicGenDataset
264	        print("Using DynamicGenDataset for data generation.")
265	
266	    else:
267	        # Use the default RLHFDataset class if no custom class is specified
268	        dataset_cls = RLHFDataset
269	    print(f"Using dataset class: {dataset_cls.__name__}")
270	
271	    # Instantiate the dataset using the determined dataset class
272	    dataset = dataset_cls(
273	        data_files=data_paths,
274	        tokenizer=tokenizer,
275	        processor=processor,
276	        config=data_config,
277	    )
278	
279	    return dataset
280	
281	
282	def create_rl_sampler(data_config, dataset):
283	    """Create a sampler for the dataset.
284	
285	    Arguments:
286	        data_config: The data config.
287	        dataset (Dataset): The dataset.
288	
289	    Returns:
290	        sampler (Sampler): The sampler.
291	    """
292	    import torch
293	    from torch.utils.data import RandomSampler, SequentialSampler
294	
295	    if data_config.sampler is not None and data_config.sampler.get("class_path", None) is not None:
296	        curriculum_class = load_extern_type(
297	            data_config.sampler.class_path,
298	            data_config.sampler.class_name,
299	        )
300	        sampler = curriculum_class(
301	            data_source=dataset,
302	            data_config=data_config,
303	        )
304	        assert isinstance(sampler, AbstractSampler)
305	        assert data_config.get("dataloader_num_workers", 8) == 0, (
306	            "If using curriculum, num_workers must be 0 to prevent data caching. "
307	            "If the dataloader caches data before the batch is done the "
308	            "curriculum sampler won't have the opportunity to reorder it. "
309	        )
310	
311	    # Use a sampler to facilitate checkpoint resumption.
312	    # If shuffling is enabled in the data configuration, create a random sampler.
313	    elif data_config.shuffle:
314	        train_dataloader_generator = torch.Generator()
315	        train_dataloader_generator.manual_seed(data_config.get("seed", 1))
316	        sampler = RandomSampler(data_source=dataset, generator=train_dataloader_generator)
317	    else:
318	        # If shuffling is disabled, use a sequential sampler to iterate through the dataset in order.
319	        sampler = SequentialSampler(data_source=dataset)
320	
321	    return sampler
322	
323	
324	if __name__ == "__main__":
325	    main()

# In PPO-Seq-MIS: log_seq_iw = sum_t (old_log_prob_t - rollout_log_prob_t)
# If this is CONSISTENTLY positive and large (~2-3 nats), 
# that means old_log_prob (actor, trained) >> rollout_log_prob (vLLM inference)
# This is a SYSTEMATIC parity mismatch, not noise.

# Let's understand what parity/sequence_log_ratio_min/max/p50 says
# parity metrics are BEFORE the update (between rollout and old_log_prob which is actor-computed)
# actor/log_seq_iw is DURING the update (old_log_prob vs rollout_log_prob)

# Let's look at the sequence log ratio mean
with open('metrics.jsonl') as f:
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in f]

rows = [r for r in rows if r['step'] > 0]
# For every step, check parity/sequence_log_ratio median vs actor/log_seq_iw_mean
print('step | par_seq_lrt_p50 | log_seq_iw_mean | par_lp_abs_mean | par_lp_abs_max')
for r in rows[:20]:
    m = r['metrics']
    step = r['step']
    p50 = m.get('parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50', float('nan'))
    iw_mean = m.get('actor/log_seq_iw_mean', float('nan'))
    lp_abs_mean = m.get('parity/logprob_abs_mean_nat', float('nan'))
    lp_abs_max = m.get('parity/logprob_abs_max_nat', float('nan'))
    print(f'{step:4d} | {p50:+.4f} | {iw_mean:+.4f} | {lp_abs_mean:.6f} | {lp_abs_max:.4f}')
" 2>&1

import json, math

# VERY IMPORTANT FINDING:
# parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50 is CONSISTENTLY NEGATIVE (~-2.3 to -2.8 nats)
# actor/log_seq_iw_mean is CONSISTENTLY POSITIVE (~+2.8 to +3.5 nats)
#
# parity_metrics computes: delta = old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs (actor_trained - vllm)
# parity/sequence_log_ratio = sum_t(delta_t) = sum_t(old_log_probs_t - rollout_log_probs_t)
#   -> NEGATIVE: rollout (vLLM) is HIGHER than actor (trained forward pass)
#
# actor/log_seq_iw_mean: log_seq_iw = sum_t(old_log_prob_t - rollout_log_prob_t)
#   -> POSITIVE: actor (trained) is HIGHER than rollout (vLLM)
#
# These are OPPOSITE SIGNS! That means the direction of the parity gap is reversed
# between parity_metrics and log_seq_iw in core_algos.
#
# Let's check the definitions:
print('Looking at run_support.py parity_metrics:')
print('  a = old_log_probs (actor, trained)')
print('  b = rollout_log_probs (vLLM inference)')
print('  delta = a - b')
print('  sums = sum_t(delta) = sum_t(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)')
print()
print('Looking at core_algos.py compute_policy_loss for PPO-Seq-MIS:')
print('  log_seq_iw = sum_t((old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob) * mask)')
print()
print('These should have the SAME SIGN at the median...')
print()
print('step | parity_sums_p50 | log_seq_iw_mean | (should be same sign!)')

rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('metrics.jsonl')]
rows = [r for r in rows if r['step'] > 0]
for r in rows[:5]:
    m = r['metrics']
    step = r['step']
    p50 = m.get('parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50')
    iw_mean = m.get('actor/log_seq_iw_mean')
    print(f'{step:4d} | {p50:+.4f} | {iw_mean:+.4f}')
" 2>&1

# Format checks enforced on CI:
# 1. Comments must appear above each field.
# 2. There must be a blank line between each field.
# 3. Inline comments (after a field on the same line) are not allowed.
# 4. Indentation level is respected for nested fields.

# specify the default per-component configs
defaults:

  # <folder_name>@<field_name>.<field_name>: <yaml_file_name>
  # actor_rollout_ref.actor: trainer/config/actor/dp_actor.yaml
  - actor@actor_rollout_ref.actor: dp_actor

  # trainer.npu_profile: trainer/config/npu_profile/npu_profile.yaml
  - npu_profile@trainer.npu_profile: npu_profile

  # data: trainer/config/data/legacy_data.yaml
  - data@data: legacy_data

  # Reference model config.
  # Reference model will be enabled when actor.use_kl_loss or/and algorithm.use_kl_in_reward is/are True.
  - ref@actor_rollout_ref.ref: dp_ref

  # Rollout model config.
  - rollout@actor_rollout_ref.rollout: rollout

  # Critic model config.
  - critic@critic: dp_critic

  # Reward model config.
  - reward_model@reward_model: dp_reward_model

  # load the reference default config, then apply the fields in the current yaml
  # self config override anything above
  - _self_

# config for actor, rollout and reference model
actor_rollout_ref:

  # Whether it's a hybrid engine, currently only supports hybrid engine
  hybrid_engine: true

  # common configs for the model
  model:

    # Huggingface model path. This can be either local path or HDFS path.
    path: ~/models/deepseek-llm-7b-chat

    # Custom chat template for the model.
    custom_chat_template: null

    # Whether to use shared memory (SHM) for accelerating the loading of model weights
    use_shm: false

    # Additional Python packages to register huggingface models/tokenizers.
    external_lib: null

    # Used to override model's original configurations, mainly dropout
    override_config: {}

    # Enable gradient checkpointing for actor
    enable_gradient_checkpointing: true

    # Enable activation offloading for actor
    enable_activation_offload: false

    # Whether to remove padding tokens in inputs during training
    use_remove_padding: false

    # Set to positive value to enable LoRA (e.g., 32)
    lora_rank: 0

    # LoRA scaling factor
    lora_alpha: 16

    # Target modules to apply LoRA. Options: "all-linear" (not recommended for VLMs) or
    # [q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj]
    target_modules: all-linear

    # Exclude modules from applying Lora. Similar usage to target_modules and Peft.
    # Example: '.*visual.*' for excluding the ViT in Qwen2.5-VL, as currently vllm does not support ViT Lora.
    exclude_modules: null

    # Whether to use Liger for linear layer fusion
    use_liger: false

    # Whether to use custom fused kernels (e.g., FlashAttention, fused MLP)
    use_fused_kernels: false

    # Options for fused kernels. If use_fused_kernels is true, this will be used.
    fused_kernel_options:

      # Implementation backend for fused kernels. Options: "triton" or "torch".
      impl_backend: torch

    # Whether to enable loading a remote code model
    trust_remote_code: false

  # Rollout model config.
  rollout:

    # may get higher throughput when set to True. When activated, Please increase max_num_batched_tokens or decrease max_model_len.
    enable_chunked_prefill: True

    # Which loader to use for rollout model weights: dummy_dtensor, hf, megatron, etc.
    # safetensors (for huge model, and set use_shm=True); dummy_dtensor: randomly init model weight
    load_format: dummy_dtensor

    # for huge model, layered summon can save memory (prevent OOM) but make it slower
    layered_summon: False

  # profiler configs
  profiler:

    # Required when using verl.utils.omega_conf_to_dataclass to instantiate dataclass configs in the entrypoint
    _target_: verl.utils.profiler.ProfilerConfig

    # True for each task has its own database, False for all tasks in one training step share one database.
    discrete: False

    # Whether to profile all ranks.
    all_ranks: False

    # The ranks that will be profiled. [] or [0,1,...]
    ranks: []

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/logs/run_001 && python3 -c "
import json, math

# CRITICAL FINDING:
# parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50 is CONSISTENTLY NEGATIVE (~-2.3 to -2.8 nats) 
# This means: sum(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs) < 0
# i.e., rollout (vLLM) has HIGHER log-probs than actor (trained forward pass)
#
# actor/log_seq_iw_mean is CONSISTENTLY POSITIVE (~+2.1 to +3.5 nats)
# This is computed as abs(sum(log_prob - rollout_log_prob)) per sequence
# (note the abs() on line 520 of dp_actor.py!)
# so it's just the magnitude, not directional
#
# So the ACTUAL direction of the gap is:
# rollout_log_prob >> old_log_prob (parity shows this consistently)
# Which means vLLM is computing much HIGHER log-probs than the FSDP actor
# for the same generated tokens.
#
# This is a consistent ~2-3 nat gap on median sequences.
# A 1500-token sequence with 0.001 nat/token average parity -> 1.5 nat total gap
# Token-level logprob abs mean is ~0.012 nats (very small), but accumulates.
#
# Wait: parity_metrics computes delta = old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs
# sums = sum_t(delta) across the sequence
# parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50 = median of sums
# This being -2.5 means: actor log-prob SUM < rollout log-prob SUM by 2.5 nats
# This is exp(-2.5) = 0.082 probability ratio per sequence
# This is NOT a large importance weight - this is NORMAL parity
# The GRPO/PPO-Seq-MIS importance weight is exp(sum(old-rollout))
# If sum(old-rollout) = -2.5, then seq_iw = exp(-2.5) = 0.082
# This would mean most sequences get nearly 0 weight!
#
# But actor/log_seq_iw_mean shows ~+2.1 (absolute value of log-seq-iw)
# That means mean |sum(log_prob - rollout_log_prob)| ≈ 2.1 nats
# And since parity shows the median of (old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob) sums is NEGATIVE,
# it's consistent: the actor diverges from rollout by ~2 nats
#
# The ESS is consistently low (0.03-0.10) which explains it:
# When seq_iw are mostly exp(-2 to -3) = 0.05-0.14, 
# the effective sample size is tiny.
#
# For PPO-Seq-MIS: sequences with seq_iw > clip_ratio_c (=3.0) are REJECTED
# seq_iw = exp(sum(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)) 
# with sum = -2.5 (parity median), exp(-2.5) = 0.082
# So most sequences have VERY LOW seq_iw (not high)
# The MIS REJECTED fraction is 0.05-0.07 (5-7%)
# These are the sequences where old >> rollout (seq_iw > 3.0, i.e., log_seq_iw > 1.1)
#
# Now: the GRPO advantage estimator is called
# Looking at metrics: 
# critic/advantages/mean = -0.055 (negative!!)
# critic/advantages/max = 0.75
# critic/advantages/min = -0.875
# The advantages are roughly symmetric around -0.055
# 
# Wait, the critic score = reward = 0.761 mean (high!)
# That means 76% of training samples are correct!
# With GRPO, advantage = (score - mean_score) / std_score
# If most samples are correct (score=1), mean is high, so many have advantage near 0
# Those with score=0 have NEGATIVE advantage
# But mean advantage is -0.055, slightly negative

rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('metrics.jsonl')]
rows = [r for r in rows if r['step'] > 0]

print('step | score_mean | adv_mean | adv_max | adv_min | clip_frac | clipfrac_lower')
for r in rows[:10]:
    m = r['metrics']
    step = r['step']
    sc = m.get('critic/score/mean', float('nan'))
    am = m.get('critic/advantages/mean', float('nan'))
    ax = m.get('critic/advantages/max', float('nan'))
    an = m.get('critic/advantages/min', float('nan'))
    cf = m.get('actor/pg_clipfrac', float('nan'))
    cl = m.get('actor/pg_clipfrac_lower', float('nan'))
    print(f'{step:4d} | {sc:.4f} | {am:+.4f} | {ax:+.4f} | {an:+.4f} | {cf:.6f} | {cl:.6f}')
" 2>&1

# When seq_iw are mostly exp(-2 to -3) = 0.05-0.14,

# But mean advantage is -0.055, slightly negative

cd /workspace/logs/run_001 && python3 -c "
import json, math

# Let me understand the parity issue more carefully.
# 
# parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50 = median(sum_t(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)) = -2.5 (negative)
# This means the FSDP actor assigns LOWER log-probs than vLLM rollout to the same tokens.
# 
# For PPO-Seq-MIS: seq_iw = exp(sum_t(old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob))
# Since sum = -2.5, seq_iw = exp(-2.5) = 0.082 for the median sequence
# 
# But in core_algos.py for PPO-Seq-MIS:
#   log_seq_iw = (old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob) * response_mask
#   log_seq_iw = log_seq_iw.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  
#   seq_iw = exp(log_seq_iw.clamp(max=20.0))
#   clip_mask = (seq_iw <= clip_ratio_c).float()
#   pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * seq_iw * clip_mask
#
# If seq_iw is 0.082, the gradient gets MULTIPLIED by 0.082 (instead of 1.0)
# This severely reduces the effective learning rate for the majority of sequences!
# 
# Only sequences where seq_iw > 3.0 (log > 1.1) are REJECTED (clipped to 0).
# Those with seq_iw < 3.0 but very small (like 0.082) contribute very weakly.
# 
# In the reference GRPO/PPO without MIS, the loss would be computed with ratio=log_prob-old_log_prob
# but here the additional multiplicative weight of seq_iw = exp(old-rollout) makes sequences
# where old << rollout contribute very weakly.
#
# The parity gap being so large and CONSISTENTLY NEGATIVE tells us:
# The actor (FSDP training) consistently assigns LOWER log-probs than vLLM rollout
# 
# This is the classic 'train-inference parity' issue. The model trained in bfloat16 FSDP
# and the vLLM rollout may differ due to different attention implementations, etc.
# But typically this gap should be small.
#
# A -2.5 nat gap over a 4000-token sequence is 0.0006 nats/token on average,
# which matches parity/logprob_abs_mean_nat ≈ 0.012 (this is the ABS mean, 
# with both positive and negative directions, so mean around 0.012 but net direction is negative)
# 
# The NET direction is: actor (FSDP) consistently has LOWER log-probs
# This means: at each token position, on average, 
# the actor assigns slightly lower probability than vLLM.
#
# Wait - but parity/logprob_abs_mean_nat ≈ 0.012 nats
# and the sequence log ratio p50 ≈ -2.5 nats for ~4000 token sequences
# That would be 2.5/4000 = 0.000625 nats/token NET signed gap
# Which is 0.000625/0.012 = 5% of the absolute mean
# So most of the absolute mismatch is NOISE, with a small but systematic BIAS.
#
# Actually the signed mean per token is parity/logprob_signed_mean_nat ≈ -0.0004
# Step 1: -0.000? Let's check
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('metrics.jsonl')]
for r in rows[:5]:
    if r['step'] == 0: continue
    m = r['metrics']
    step = r['step']
    signed = m.get('parity/logprob_signed_mean_nat')
    abs_mean = m.get('parity/logprob_abs_mean_nat')
    seq_p50 = m.get('parity/sequence_log_ratio_p50')
    tokens = m.get('parity/tokens')
    seqs = m.get('parity/sequences')
    print(f'step {step}: signed={signed:.6f}, abs_mean={abs_mean:.6f}, seq_p50={seq_p50:.4f}, tokens={tokens}, seqs={seqs}')
    if tokens and signed:
        expected_p50 = signed * (tokens/seqs) if seqs else 0
        print(f'  expected seq_sum from signed_mean: {expected_p50:.4f} (vs actual p50: {seq_p50:.4f})')
" 2>&1

import json, math

# CONFIRMED FINDING:
# parity/logprob_signed_mean_nat = -0.000476 nats/token (consistently negative)
# This is a SYSTEMATIC BIAS: actor(FSDP) gives lower log-probs than rollout(vLLM)
# Over a 4000-token sequence, this accumulates to -0.000476 * 4000 = -1.9 nats
# Which matches the sequence_log_ratio_p50 of -2.9
# 
# This consistent parity gap means:
# seq_iw = exp(sum(old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob)) = exp(-2.9) ≈ 0.055 for median sequence
# 
# In PPO-Seq-MIS: 
#   pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * seq_iw * clip_mask
# The loss for each sequence gets multiplied by ~0.055
# This SEVERELY ATTENUATES the gradient signal!
# 
# The effective learning rate is reduced by factor of ~0.055 for the median sequence.
# Most sequences have very small importance weights.
# This explains the slow training progress (AIME barely improves from 0.22 to 0.28 over 440 steps)
#
# However, the question is: is this a DEFECT in the code or just a consequence of 
# the inherent parity gap between FSDP actor and vLLM rollout?
#
# Let me check whether norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo matters here.
# The issue might be elsewhere. Let me look at the specific configuration...
# 
# Actually, the key diagnostic: the launch.json says:
# 'actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss.algo=PPO-Seq-MIS'
# 
# In core_algos.py for PPO-Seq-MIS (line 809-811):
# elif algo == 'PPO-Seq-MIS':
#     clip_mask = (seq_iw <= clip_ratio_c).float()
#     pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * seq_iw * clip_mask
#
# seq_iw = exp(sum(old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob))
# Since old_log_prob is SMALLER than rollout_log_prob (by ~2.5 nats),
# seq_iw = exp(-2.5) ≈ 0.08
#
# The design intent of MIS is to WEIGHT sequences by pi_old/pi_rollout
# When old is CLOSE to rollout, weight should be ~1.0
# When old >> rollout, weight is > 1 (and gets clipped at clip_ratio_c)
# When old << rollout, weight is < 1 (and reduces gradient contribution)
#
# The issue: in a healthy run, after the first update, old_log_prob SHOULD BE 
# computed by the actor AFTER the update, while rollout_log_prob was computed
# during generation BEFORE the update. So old > rollout is expected.
#
# But here, old < rollout (consistently negative).
# This means the actor (FSDP) assigns LOWER probs than vLLM for the SAME tokens.
# 
# Let me check: when are old_log_probs computed vs rollout_log_probs?
# From ray_trainer.py:
# 1. rollout: vLLM generates AND computes log_probs (rollout_log_probs)
# 2. old_log_prob: actor FSDP recomputes log_probs of rollout sequences
# 3. These are computed at the SAME policy state (before any update)
# So old_log_prob should MATCH rollout_log_prob closely (parity test)
#
# The SIGN matters: old_log_prob should be close to rollout_log_prob
# A systematic negative bias means FSDP computes lower probs than vLLM
# This IS the parity issue being tracked by parity_metrics
#
# But is this causing a defect? The parity gap of -0.0005 nats/token 
# seems small but accumulates. Let me look at whether there's a bug 
# that would cause this to be artificially large.
#
# Wait - let me re-read parity_metrics more carefully!
# In run_support.py:
#   a = batch.batch['old_log_probs']  (computed by FSDP actor AFTER update at step N-1)
#   b = batch.batch['rollout_log_probs']  (computed by vLLM during generation at step N)
#   delta = a - b
# 
# WAIT! 'old_log_probs' in parity_metrics is the actor log probs AFTER SOME UPDATES,
# and 'rollout_log_probs' is from the CURRENT rollout.
# The parity metrics are computed in _compute_old_log_prob() in ray_trainer.py
# which is called AFTER generation but BEFORE updating.
# So old_log_probs here = CURRENT actor (before this step's update)
# And rollout_log_probs = current generation
#
# Since they should match closely (both at the same model state), 
# the parity gap reflects actual numerical differences.
# A systematic -0.0005/token gap over 4000 tokens = -2 nats is real.
#
# Actually let me look deeper at whether the signed_mean being negative
# reveals something about the normalization or temperature settings.
# Check the temperature used in rollout vs actor.
print('Looking at temperature settings...')
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('metrics.jsonl')]
r1 = rows[1]  # step 1
print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in r1['metrics'].items() if 'temp' in k.lower()}, indent=2))
" 2>&1

# Format checks enforced on CI:
# 1. Comments must appear above each field.
# 2. There must be a blank line between each field.
# 3. Inline comments (after a field on the same line) are not allowed.
# 4. Indentation level is respected for nested fields.

# defaults specify the default config from each component
defaults:

  # dp actor config, inheriting from trainer/config/actor/actor.yaml
  - actor

  # load the reference default config, then apply the fields in the current yaml
  - _self_

# TODO(haibin.lin): switch to fsdp2
strategy: fsdp2

# Gradient clipping for actor updates, specific to the strategy.
grad_clip: 1.0

# Sequence parallelism size for Ulysses-style model parallelism
# oc.select: the default val for ref.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
ulysses_sequence_parallel_size: 1

# calculate entropy with chunking to reduce memory peak
entropy_from_logits_with_chunking: False

# recompute entropy
entropy_checkpointing: False

# optimizer configs
optim:

  # Warmup steps; negative value delegates to lr_warmup_steps_ratio
  lr_warmup_steps: -1

  # Minimum LR ratio for cosine schedule
  min_lr_ratio: 0.0

  # Number of cosine cycles in LR schedule
  num_cycles: 0.5

  # LR warmup style: "constant" or "cosine"
  warmup_style: constant

# configs for FSDP
fsdp_config:

  # policy for wrapping the model
  wrap_policy:

    # Minimum number of parameters to trigger wrapping a layer with FSDP
    min_num_params: 0

  # Whether to offload model parameters to CPU (trades speed for memory)
  param_offload: false

  # Whether to offload optimizer state to CPU
  optimizer_offload: false

  # Only for FSDP2: offload param/grad/optimizer during train
  offload_policy: false

  # Only for FSDP2: Reshard after forward pass to reduce memory footprint
  reshard_after_forward: true

  # Number of GPUs in each FSDP shard group; -1 means auto
  fsdp_size: -1

  # Only for FSDP1: FSDP1 configuration, prefetch the next forward-pass all-gather
  # before the current forward computation.
  forward_prefetch: False

# Format checks enforced on CI:
# 1. Comments must appear above each field.
# 2. There must be a blank line between each field.
# 3. Inline comments (after a field on the same line) are not allowed.
# 4. Indentation level is respected for nested fields.

# the abstract actor configs
# fsdp, fsdp2 or megatron. must be set.
strategy: ???

# Split each sample into sub-batches of this size for PPO
ppo_mini_batch_size: 256

# [Deprecated] Global micro batch size
ppo_micro_batch_size: null

# Local per-GPU micro batch size
ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu: null

# Whether to automatically adjust batch size at runtime
# oc.select: the default val for ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz
use_dynamic_bsz: false

# Max tokens per GPU in one PPO batch; affects gradient accumulation
# Typically it should be: n * ${data.max_prompt_length} + ${data.max_response_length}
# oc.select: the default val for ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu
ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu: 16384

# PPO clip ratio
clip_ratio: 0.2

# Lower bound for asymmetric clipping (used in dual-clip PPO)
clip_ratio_low: 0.2

# Upper bound for asymmetric clipping (used in dual-clip PPO)
clip_ratio_high: 0.2

# policy loss config
policy_loss:

  # Loss function mode: vanilla / clip-cov / kl-cov /gpg from https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22617
  loss_mode: "vanilla"
  algo: "PPO"

  # Ratio of tokens to be clipped for clip-cov loss
  clip_cov_ratio: 0.0002

  # Lower bound for clip-cov loss
  clip_cov_lb: 1.0

  # Upper bound for clip-cov loss
  clip_cov_ub: 5.0

  # Ratio of tokens to be applied kl penalty for kl-cov loss
  kl_cov_ratio: 0.0002

  # KL divergence penalty coefficient
  ppo_kl_coef: 0.1

# Constant C in Dual-clip PPO; clips when advantage < 0 and ratio > C
clip_ratio_c: 3.0

# Loss aggregation mode: "token-mean", "seq-mean-token-sum", or "seq-mean-token-mean"
loss_agg_mode: "seq-mean-token-sum-norm"
dtype: float16

# Entropy regularization coefficient in PPO loss
entropy_coeff: 0

# Whether to use KL loss instead of KL reward penalty. True for GRPO
use_kl_loss: false

# Whether to use torch.compile()
# oc.select: the default val for ref.use_torch_compile
use_torch_compile: true

# KL loss coefficient when use_kl_loss is enabled. For GRPO
kl_loss_coef: 0.001

# Type of KL divergence loss. Options: "kl"(k1), "abs", "mse"(k2), "low_var_kl"(k3), "full"
kl_loss_type: low_var_kl

# Number of PPO epochs per batch
ppo_epochs: 1

# Shuffle training data across PPO epochs
shuffle: false

# checkpoint configs
checkpoint:

  # What to include in saved checkpoints
  # with 'hf_model' you can save whole model as hf format, now only use sharded model checkpoint to save space
  save_contents: ['model', 'optimizer', 'extra']

  # For more flexibility, you can specify the contents to load from the checkpoint.
  # .xxx refers to the local variable xxx from the same level of hierarchy similar to python pkg
  load_contents: ${.save_contents}

# optimizer configs
optim:

  # Learning rate
  lr: 1e-6

  # Warmup steps ratio (used if lr_warmup_steps is negative)
  lr_warmup_steps_ratio: 0.0

  # Total training steps (must be overridden at runtime)
  total_training_steps: -1

  # Weight decay
  weight_decay: 0.0
  betas: [0.9, 0.95]
  eps: 1e-15
